formulas.title: Liquid and injection dose
formulas.meaning: Works out how many ml to give when the medicine comes as a liquid or an injection.
formulas.keywords: syrup suspension injection ml volume dose

example.question: Ordered 500 mg. Stock 1000 mg in 2 ml.

formulas.tip: Make the units match before you divide.

formulas.title: Tablet dose
formulas.meaning: Works out how many tablets to give.
formulas.keywords: tablet capsule oral number of tablets
formulas.tip: Tablets are usually given whole or as a half. If you get something else, check again.

formulas.title: Weight-based dose
formulas.meaning: Some doses depend on how much the patient weighs. The order is written as mg per kg.
formulas.keywords: weight kg mg/kg child paediatric pediatric body weight

example.question: Ordered 15 mg per kg. The patient weighs 20 kg.

formulas.tip: Check the weight is in kg, not pounds or grams.

formulas.title: Weight units: kg, g, mg, mcg
formulas.meaning: To go to a smaller unit, multiply by 1000. To go to a bigger unit, divide by 1000.
formulas.keywords: convert conversion gram milligram microgram kilogram mcg mg g kg

example.question: Change 0.25 g to mg.
steps: g to mg is a smaller unit, so multiply by 1000

formulas.tip: Going the other way: 500 mcg ÷ 1000 = 0.5 mg.

formulas.title: Volume units: litres and ml
formulas.meaning: To change litres to ml, multiply by 1000. To change ml to litres, divide by 1000.
formulas.keywords: convert conversion litre liter ml millilitre volume
formulas.tip: Going the other way: 250 ml ÷ 1000 = 0.25 L.

formulas.title: Pounds to kilograms
formulas.meaning: Dose calculations need kg. 1 kg is about 2.2 lb.

example.question: A patient weighs 132 lb. How many kg?

formulas.tip: Always write the unit next to your answer.

formulas.title: Hours and minutes
formulas.meaning: Drip rate formulas often need time in minutes. Multiply hours by 60.
formulas.tip: Going the other way: 90 minutes ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours.

formulas.title: Flow rate in ml per hour
formulas.meaning: Works out how fast a drip or pump must run to give the fluid in the time ordered.
formulas.keywords: iv drip rate infusion ml per hour fluids pump
formulas.tip: Check the time is in hours.

formulas.title: Time for an infusion
formulas.meaning: Works out how long a bag will take to finish at a given rate.
formulas.keywords: iv infusion duration how long finish time fluids
formulas.tip: Change the answer to hours and minutes if it is not a whole number.

formulas.title: Drops per minute
formulas.formula: Drops per minute = Volume (ml) × Drop factor ÷ Time (minutes)
formulas.meaning: The drop factor is how many drops make 1 ml. It is printed on the giving set packet.
formulas.keywords: iv drip drops per minute gtt drop factor giving set fluids

example.question: 1000 ml over 10 hours. Drop factor 15 drops per ml.

formulas.tip: Use time in minutes. Round to the nearest whole drop.

formulas.title: Drops per minute from ml per hour
formulas.formula: Drops per minute = ml per hour × Drop factor ÷ 60
formulas.meaning: A shortcut when you already know the flow rate in ml/hr.
formulas.keywords: iv drip drops per minute gtt drop factor ml per hour fluids

example.question: Rate 120 ml/hr. Drop factor 20 drops per ml.

formulas.tip: Check the drop factor on the giving set packet.

formulas.title: Concentration
formulas.meaning: Tells you how much medicine is in each ml.
formulas.keywords: concentration strength mg per ml amount volume

example.question: 500 mg in 10 ml. How many mg in each ml?

formulas.tip: You can also find the dose: ordered ÷ concentration. For 200 mg: 200 ÷ 50 = 4 ml.

formulas.title: Percentage strength
formulas.formula: x% means x g in 100 ml
formulas.meaning: A percentage on a fluid label tells you how many grams are in 100 ml.
formulas.keywords: percentage percent % solution strength saline dextrose

example.question: Sodium chloride 0.9%. How many mg in 100 ml?

formulas.tip: So 1 litre of 0.9% has 9 g, because 1 litre is 10 times 100 ml.

formulas.title: Ratio strength
formulas.meaning: A ratio like 1:1000 means 1 g of medicine in that many ml.

example.question: A solution is 1:1000. How many mg in each ml?
steps: 1 g = 1000 mg, so 1000 mg in 1000 ml

formulas.tip: Change grams to mg first, then divide.
